subject: MAP close slippage: dual-path replan & risk triage
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Barnes <kevin.barnes@acmecorp.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP close slippage: initial signal

Kevin / Acme team —

Quick note from our side: we saw the acceptance window on the MAP slip by two business weeks after your QA scheduling shifted. We want to avoid a hard go-live delay, so propose we triage along two parallel paths (details below) and lock updated owners in the MAP today.

Immediate ask: can you confirm which acceptance tests are now blocked by QA scheduling vs procurement approvals by EOD PDT? That will let us choose the right path.

Proposed dual-path sketch (brief):
- Fast path (target go-live: original date + 1 week) — aggressive QA support from Acme, Redwood provides a hotfix branch and night-owl benching, procurement to prioritize remaining PO sign-off.
- Stable path (target go-live: original date + 3 weeks) — staggered cutover, additional regression, and post-cutover rollback window, procurement + legal sign-off required.

I'll attach an updated MAP and a short risk log once I validate owners. If you prefer a single path, call it out and we'll rebaseline formally.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP with owners), close_risk_log.csv (current risk register)

From: Kevin Barnes <kevin.barnes@acmecorp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP close slippage: initial signal

Soojin —

Thanks for the heads up. Short answer: QA was bumped because our security team found a blocking telemetry gap during the eval. Procurement is ready to sign but needs updated service dates in the SOW before routing.

We prefer the stable path given the telemetry ask, but appreciate a fast path contingency if Security greenlights the telemetry change earlier today. Can you share the MAP with explicit sign-off milestones (legal, security, procurement, QA) and an updated timeline?

-Kevin
Kevin Barnes
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corporation

>

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Barnes <kevin.barnes@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-30T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP close slippage: dual-path replan proposal

Kevin — thanks for the quick context. Per your note, stable path looks prudent but we want a concurrent fast-path contingency to preserve flexibility. I attached MAP_v2.xlsx and close_risk_log.csv (stubs). Key highlights and asks: 

1) Explicit milestones (map columns in attached):
   - Legal sign-off (target owner: Acme Legal) — required for PO terms change; deadline request: 2025-09-02 17:00 PDT
   - Security acceptance gate (owner: Acme Security) — telemetry acceptance or mitigation sign-off; deadline request: 2025-09-01 12:00 PDT
   - QA acceptance window (owner: Acme QA) — if blockers persist, shift to stable path; deadline request: 2025-09-03 09:00 PDT

2) Risk log snapshot (see attached):
   - R1: Telemetry gap (impact: high) — mitigation: Redwood will instrument additional no-op telemetry in staging and share logs within 24h for review. Owner: Redwood Eng (Rishi).
   - R2: PO date mismatch (impact: medium) — mitigation: Redwood to provide revised SOW template; owner: Acme Procurement.
   - R3: Regression surface from hotfix branch (impact: medium) — mitigation: extended smoke window and rollback plan. Owner: Redwood SE (Laura).

3) Dual-path operational triggers (in plain terms):
   - If Security signs telemetry change by 2025-09-01 12:00 PDT -> execute Fast path (go-live target: 2025-09-08).
   - If Security does not sign -> Stable path (go-live target: 2025-09-22) with staged cutover and 7-day rollback hold.

4) Next steps (clear asks):
   - Acme Security: confirm sign/deny timeline for telemetry (reply by 2025-09-01 12:00 PDT).
   - Acme Procurement: confirm whether updated SOW template is sufficient for routing (reply by 2025-09-02 17:00 PDT).
   - Acme QA: share list of blocked test cases (reply by 2025-09-03 09:00 PDT).

If you agree, we'll treat the Stable path as default and only flip to Fast if the Security trigger is met. I recommend Jordan be looped for a procurement prioritization ask if we see further slippage.

Best —
Soojin
Attachment stubs: MAP_v2.xlsx, close_risk_log.csv

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Quick note from the eng side: we'll stand up the additional instrumentation in staging this afternoon and push logs to the shared drive. I'll be the owner for R1 and will ping Kevin directly if anything looks off.

-Rishi

Subject: Re: MAP close slippage: dual-path replan & risk triage

Good plan — solid dual-path framing. Two items from my side: 

1) I'll escalate to Acme procurement and ask they route the revised SOW as an expedited change (I can signal priority). Laura, please prepare the SOW redline and a short cover note for procurement routing.
2) If Security wants additional evidence beyond the telemetry logs, we should offer a short joint session (Redwood + Acme Security) tomorrow to walk through the instrumentation and acceptance criteria.

Treat my reply as approval to proceed with the Stable path as the default and to stand up the contingency. Keep the thread minimal for audit purposes — capture decisions in the MAP_v2.xlsx and we'll attach to the HubSpot deal record.

-Jordan
VP, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
